subject: Reserved GPU fit for real-time NLU pipeline - post-demo recap & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@lexiai.com>, Samir Desai <samir@lexiai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved GPU fit for real-time NLU pipeline - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Elena / Samir — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed path forward.

TL;DR recommendation: Dedicated (reserved) capacity for the real-time NLU endpoints, with a short 2-week POC to validate H100 vs A100 economics and latency at your token mix. Hosted API is a fallback for spikes and early integration, Private (VPC) can follow if procurement requires on-prem/VPC isolation.

What we heard on the call (please correct any numbers):
- Production traffic shape: 120 TPS steady-state, up to ~300 TPS peak bursts.
- Typical request size: ~300–400 tokens (mixed short prompts + full-document context).
- Latency SLO: 90% < 120ms token latency (developer dashboard target).
- Multi-region not required for initial rollout (US primary).

Primary sizing questions / what we need to size a reserved pool:
1) Confirm sustained TPS (120) vs peak TPS (300) and expected burst duration (minutes vs hours).
2) Confirm concurrency model: are requests single-shot or streaming? Any long-lived chat sessions?
3) Send a small sample token-profile (distribution of 0–64 / 65–256 / 257–1024 token requests) — attached is a suggested CSV template.
4) Any mandatory GPU flavor preferences (H100 / A100 / L40) or hard budget constraint for monthly GPU costs?

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- You: share the token profile CSV and confirm burst window (end of day Fri).
- Us: run a quick perf sweep (1–2 days) across H100/A100 quantized configs and share a throughput/latency matrix.
- Us: propose a 2-week dedicated POC with a small reserved pool (2 GPUs) + hosted overflow to validate 95/99 latency and cost.

Attachments: capacity-worksheet.xlsx (blank worksheet for your token distribution), token_profile.csv (example).

If that plan sounds OK I'll schedule the perf sweep and ping engineering to prepare the POC template.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0127
https://redwoodinference.com

From: Elena Torres <elena@lexiai.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@lexiai.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 19:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU fit for real-time NLU pipeline - post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Olga — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed steady-state ~120 TPS, peak bursts to ~300 TPS lasting ~10–20 minutes when we run batch-affinity jobs (not constant).
- Concurrency: mostly single-shot REST calls (no streaming for now). We do sometimes open long sessions for customer support transcripts (~1–2% of traffic) but those are low QPS.
- Token mix: attaching a small sample export (token_profile.csv) — distribution included.
- GPU preference: we'd like to understand H100 vs A100 TCO. If H100 gives latency headroom we care about that, but price delta matters.
- Procurement: procurement@lexiai.com is on copy; procurement prefers a 30-day pilot before committing to reserved monthly capacity.

Questions for you: can the POC use a reserved pool with autoscaling to 4 GPUs during sustained bursts? Also need an initial ballpark for monthly reserved costs including expected egress and support add-ons.

Elena Torres
CTO, LexiAI
elena@lexiai.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@lexiai.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU fit for real-time NLU pipeline - post-demo recap & next steps

Elena — got the token sample, thanks. Quick technical notes based on the CSV and the call:

- Observed token distribution (from the attached sample): ~55% <=128 tokens, 35% between 129–512, 10% >512. That profile is favorable for higher batch efficiency but the 10% long-context requests will drive KV cache pressure.
- For your latency SLO and 120 TPS steady-state, H100s give ~30–40% headroom at typical quantized 4-bit runs; A100s can hit the numbers but will sit closer to saturation unless we run more aggressive quantization.
- Autoscale behavior: we can configure reserved pools to scale up to 4 GPUs within ~60–90s for sustained bursts (10–20 min bursts look ideal for this). For 10–20 minute bursts we recommend a burst policy that pre-warms an extra GPU when burst starts to keep p95 latency low.

A few items we need to finalize the POC:
- Confirm whether you want H100 for the POC or want us to test both H100/A100 during the perf sweep.
- Any hard limit on monthly spend for the pilot (so we size the pool accordingly).
- If you plan to run quantized models (4-bit), any constraints on acceptable quality delta vs FP16? We can run A/B evals on your prompt set.

If you approve, I'll schedule the perf sweep right after we confirm the GPU flavor choices.

- Rishi
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwoodinference.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@lexiai.com>, Samir Desai <samir@lexiai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@lexiai.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU fit for real-time NLU pipeline - post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks for the sample and clarity, Elena. Proposed minimal POC that matches procurement's ask (30 days) and gives the engineering team measurable numbers:

POC outline (30-day):
- Reserved pool: 2 H100s for baseline (dedicated), autoscale policy to add up to 2 additional H100s for sustained bursts (total 4).
- Overflow: Hosted API fallback for rare 500+ TPS spikes to avoid request throttling.
- Tests we run: load profile (steady 120 TPS), burst test to 300 TPS for 20 minutes, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and quality regression check (we'll run your prompt set with quantized and FP16 variants).
- Deliverables: throughput/latency matrix, cost estimate (monthly pro-rata for reserved hours), and recommended production GPU mix for scale.

Pricing note (ballpark for evaluation):
- H100 reserved baseline (2 GPUs) + support + egress estimate: we'll send a formal quote but ballpark $XXk–$YYk/mo depending on region and support level — I'll have Sales ops produce exact numbers once you confirm POC scope.

Next actions:
1) Elena / procurement: confirm "POC scope: 30 days, 2H100 baseline + autoscale to 4" and any hard monthly cap (reply to this thread).
2) LexiAI: sign the short POC MSA we will send (DocuSign link to follow).
3) Rishi / infra: I'll kick off the perf sweep (H100 vs A100) the moment we have confirmation.

Shared sheet with the proposed schedule and responsibilities: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBqExampleSharedSheet

Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

OK — procurement confirms we can proceed with a 30-day POC. We approve the 2 H100 baseline + autoscale to 4. No hard monthly cap at procurement level for the pilot, procurement asks for the formal quote to attach to the MSA.

Please include SOC2 report and a short runbook for incident escalation as part of the deliverables. Let's aim to kick off next Monday (Dec 27) so we have the week to finish internal approvals.

Elena
